claim_ceiling: This eliminates every proof that tries to choose a straight segment between two roots. It does not exclude a broken-line path and does not solve Erdős #1041.

critical_point_hub_repair.length_argument: the two radial legs each have length r, so total length 2r<2
critical_point_hub_repair.meaning: The cubic kills every direct chord but admits a short two-segment path through its critical point.

analytic_bridge.falsification_consequence: Any general proof must leave the single-chord geometry; the same cubic keeps critical-point hubs and more general paths live.
analytic_bridge.survival_consequence: If some pair were safe, isolate its symmetry-breaking feature as a candidate root-selection lemma.

experiment_contract.authority_boundary: Experiment metadata and finite computation are evidence, not proof authority; claim status changes only through Lean, an exact counterexample, or the named owner verifier.

hypothesis.statement: Every monic polynomial with roots in the open unit disk has two roots whose straight segment is contained in |f|<1.

probe.computation: Evaluate z^3-r^3 exactly in Q(omega) at all three pair midpoints for r=99/100.
probe.falsifier: One pair midpoint with polynomial modulus at most one, or one root outside the open unit disk.
probe.question: Can a symmetric cubic force every straight root-pair midpoint outside the strict unit lemniscate?
probe.stop_condition: After all three exact midpoint evaluations agree and exceed one, retire every straight-root-pair proof geometry.

problem.claim_ceiling: The exact cubic eliminates straight root-pair segments only; critical-point hubs, multi-segment, curved, and topological routes remain open.
problem.target_statement: Find two roots joined by a curve of length less than two inside the strict unit lemniscate.

result.summary: For f(z)=z^3-(99/100)^3, all three roots lie in the open unit disk, but every distinct root pair has midpoint value -9(99/100)^3/8, whose modulus is greater than one. Thus every straight root-pair segment exits the strict unit lemniscate.
